reviewer: off-schedule panel — 3 trainers + head coach, convened at your request, NOT the 6 AM automatic review
brief: Start with the thing that costs you something. On Monday 17 August the app was going to cut every weight in your program by twenty percent and about forty percent of your sets, for seven days, on its own — the back-off week is written into the plan and it fires on a date, not on how you have been training. The program trainer ruled today that it should not run as written. A back-off exists to shed the fatigue of a block of hard training, and the block it was written for is thirteen lifting nights that all happened between 20 July and 3 August; the eleven days you have just had already did that job. Running it would have you lift twenty percent under weights you last touched on 3 August and start the next block detrained. His call was to keep building through 23 August, start Meso 2 on the 24th exactly as planned, and let the back-off already booked for 21-27 September be the first one — nothing later in the calendar moves, and the show is still 199 days out. You approved that, and it is done: Meso 1 now ends on 23 August and the deload week is out of the program, so nothing will drop your weights on Monday. Meso 1 reads week 4 of 5 instead of 4 of 4, which is the extra week you just gained. Second thing, and you should know it: this same trainer raised this on 9 August and you never saw it, because that morning's review was never committed to the app. Tonight is Push A, because you set it by hand. Nothing new has been logged since 3 August, so no number on this card is built on anything newer than that, and the panel deliberately did not invent progress out of an eleven-day gap it cannot measure. Four lifts repeat 31 July exactly: incline 150, 170, 170, then 175 — six, six, six and the seven you already own, not a rep more on a cold first night back. Crossover 13.75 and 15 for fourteen, thirteen, thirteen. Shoulder press keeps the 35 opener then the two 40s, same as that night. Overhead triceps keeps 53.75 to open, then 55 twice, and the 57.5 that gave you eight reps in a ten-to-twelve slot is gone. Two lifts go up because you earned them outright and the layoff does not take that back: chest press 157.5, 165, 172.5 for ten — you finished 12, 12, 12 at the weights below those, which is the top of the range on every set — and lateral raise at 10. That 10 is not a cut from 10.5: 10.5 is not a weight that machine can make, it is the same setting you have been using, and the card now prints what is actually on the pin. One lift comes down properly. Rope pushdown goes to 52.5. Your last six sets there were eight, seven, nine and eight, seven, eight against a slot asking for at least ten, and on 31 July you stripped it mid-session — the weight was wrong, not you, and 52.5 is the first setting below everything that has failed. Face pulls are not raised, and the panel ruled them optional tonight. You have objected to that lift in writing twice, and the card in your queue that swaps it for the reverse pec deck is the one that settles it for good. Which brings up the four cards sitting unanswered on your plan screen — rope pushdown's rep range, the face-pull swap, straight-arm pulldown, and calf raises. Three of them are fixes to complaints you wrote yourself. They take under a minute. Last, unchanged and still true: one bodyweight reading since 4 January and one cardio session in the whole log. You told the panel you have been running and playing basketball, which is more conditioning than the log has ever seen — none of it is written down, so none of it counts toward anything, and the scale is still the cheapest thing you can do for March.

flags.note: The 17-23 August back-off is gone — you approved the ruling and it is out of the program. Meso 1 now runs to 23 August, Meso 2 still starts on the 24th, and your first back-off week is 21-27 September.
The 9 August review, which first raised the back-off question, was never committed to the app — you never saw it. The question reached you five days late.
Tonight is Push A because you set it by hand. Nothing has been logged since 3 August, so every number here is built on that date or earlier.
Face pulls are not raised tonight and the panel ruled them optional — the swap card in your queue decides whether they stay on Push A at all.
Four program cards are still unanswered on your plan screen. Three of them are fixes to complaints you wrote in the log yourself.
One bodyweight reading since 4 January and one logged cardio session in the whole block. The running and basketball you did are not in the log, so nothing counts them.

proposals.why: Still open and unanswered, and it is on tonight's card: Push A's rope pushdown asks ten to twelve and your six sets there came in at eight, seven, nine and eight, seven, eight — not one set inside the range all block, so the weight can never move, and twelve to fifteen makes it a slot you can actually finish.

Still open and unanswered, and it is also on tonight's card: Push A is the last place face pulls are still in your week, and it is the one prescription you have objected to in writing twice — "I did angels and demons instead" on 28 July and "Do you have a brain?" on 31 July — so this puts the reverse pec deck in that slot instead, two sets of twelve to fifteen. Same back of the shoulder, and it is the machine you have carried from 82.5 to 90 without missing a set.

Still open — you have not had a session since this went on your card: both your last two Pull B nights sat at 37.5 and finished 13, 11, 12 and 13, 12, 12 — never the fifteen this slot asks for, so the weight can never move, and asking ten to twelve means the twelves you already do earn the next step.

Still open and unanswered, and this is not the cut to two sets you declined on 3 August — it is three: Legs A asks for four and you have done two, two and three, and because the weight only moves when you finish every set the plan asks for, three makes the prescription the work you actually do.

overrides.reason: Exactly 31 July: 150, 170, 170, then 175 for the seven you already own. Two trainers split on this — one wanted a seventh rep on all four sets, the other wanted the night repeated as logged. On your first night back after eleven days, on the heaviest press you do, you get the night I can actually see. The extra rep is still there in two weeks.

Up 7.5 on every set, and this one is not affected by the time off. You did 150, 157.5 and 165 for twelve, twelve and twelve on 31 July — the top of the range on every single set, which is the whole test — and you pressed 165, 172.5 and 180 on this machine on 3 August. Nothing here is new ground.

Same two settings as 31 July for the same reps: fourteen, thirteen, thirteen. This lift has genuinely stalled and it will need a way out, but the first night back after eleven days is not where you go looking for it.

The 35 opener stays, then the two 40s — 31 July repeated. The trainers split: you did beat 35 by two reps that night, which normally kills the opener, but this is the least supported lift on the card and you have to clean the bells into position cold. Take the opener back next Push A, once there is a logged night behind you.

53.75 to open, then 55 twice, and 57.5 is off the card — it gave you eight reps in a slot asking for ten to twelve on 31 July. You ran 55 for eleven, eleven and ten on 3 August, so the two top sets are a weight you have just done.

10 for thirteen across. Read this once: 10.5 is not a setting that machine can make — the pin is 7.5 and the add-on plate is 2.5, which is 10, and that is what you have actually been lifting. The number on the card changed; the weight in your hand did not.

Down to 52.5. Your last six sets here were eight, seven, nine and eight, seven, eight against a slot asking for at least ten, and on 31 July you stripped it mid-session. Both trainers agreed it comes down and split only on how far — 52.5 is the first setting below every weight that has failed, so it is the one that gets you back inside the range.

Held exactly where it was on 31 July, and not raised. One trainer argued for more weight; the other said skip it tonight, and that side won — you have objected to this lift in writing twice. The swap card in your queue is what settles whether it stays on Push A at all.

dissent.progression: Hold the weights but ask a seventh rep on all four sets — the last night came in at the bottom of the range.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 31 July set for set: 6, 6, 6 and the 7 he already owns, because every number on this card is fourteen days old and the eleven days between are unmeasured.
dissent.why: Recovery. This is the heaviest press in the program on the first logged night back, and progression's own case for the extra rep rests on a rep he has never hit at 170. Repeating a night the log can prove costs nothing and asks for nothing he has not already done. The step is available again the moment there is one logged session behind him.

dissent.progression: Same pins, one more rep on each set — 15, 14, 14.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 31 July exactly — 14, 13, 13 — because nothing newer exists to justify a move.
dissent.why: Recovery, and for the same reason as the incline: consistency matters more here than one rep. Progression is right that this lift is stuck and will need a real intervention, but the way out of a stall is not the first night back from eleven days off. Ruled with the incline so the whole card tells one story.

dissent.progression: All three sets at 40 — he took 35 for twelve reps in an eight-to-ten slot, which makes the opener provably too light.
dissent.recovery: Keep the 35 opener, then the two 40s: least supported lift of the night, bells cleaned into position, first night back.
dissent.why: Recovery, narrowly. Progression's arithmetic is correct — 35 for twelve in an eight-to-ten slot is a beaten set and normally the opener dies for it. But the ramp 35, 40, 40 is exactly what he did on 31 July, the two working sets are untouched either way, and the risk on this lift is getting the bells overhead cold, not the pressing. The earned step goes on next Push A's card.

dissent.progression: 55 across all three sets — drop the 57.5, but bring the opener up to match.
dissent.recovery: Keep the 53.75 opener and run 55 twice, exactly the two settings he used on 31 July.
dissent.why: Recovery. Both seats agree the 57.5 goes, which is the decision that mattered. On the opener, recovery's version is what the log actually shows, and raising an opener on a night where the whole card is deliberately repeating is the kind of small inconsistency that makes a card argue with itself.

dissent.progression: Cut to 55 for eleven, ten, ten.
dissent.recovery: Cut to 52.5 for twelve, eleven, ten — 55 is a weight that has already failed to clear the floor.
dissent.why: Recovery, on the evidence. The point of this cut is to get him back inside a ten-to-twelve slot, and 55 for eight reps on 31 July is one of the sets that missed it. Cutting to a weight that has already failed would leave the same problem with a smaller number on it.

dissent.progression: Push — add the 1.25 micro to 28.75 after three straight nights of fifteen and fifteen.
dissent.recovery: Skip it tonight. He wrote "Do you have a brain?" next to this lift on 31 July and objected to it again on 28 July.
dissent.why: Recovery. Progression read the reps correctly and, seeing no notes by design, could not know it was arguing to add weight to the one prescription he has rejected in writing twice. The packet holds it at 31 July's numbers rather than removing it outright, because removing it is his call and the swap card that does it properly is already in his queue.
